steps.say: A child who strokes every time she cries has a plumbing problem, not bad luck. Hyperventilation constricts already starving vessels.
steps.tx: **Moyamoya disease** (smoke vessel illness) shows bilateral terminal carotid stenosis with a **puff-of-smoke collateral** (smoky bypass network) on angiography, graded by **Suzuki staging** (six stage scale) from I to VI (stages 1 to 6), and **RNF213 mutation** (gene defect) links the East Asian familial form seen in young Indian case series too.

steps.say: Age flips the presentation. Crying triggers ischaemia in children while fragile collaterals bleed in adults.
steps.tx: Children present with **ischaemic strokes** (blocked blood attacks) or **transient ischaemic attack** (brief warning strokes) triggered by crying and **hyperventilation** (fast breathing), while adults bleed from fragile collaterals, so presentation alone often suggests the age group before angiography confirms the **Suzuki stage** (disease stage), with transient attacks often stereotyped and brief.

vis.alt: Axial brain sections comparing epidural haematoma, subdural haematoma, subarachnoid haemorrhage and ischaemic stroke.
vis.caption: Ischaemic stroke pattern in a child with a narrowed cerebral circulation. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: New pipes beat medicines here. Direct bypass plus indirect ingrowth together keep the brain perfused through childhood.
steps.tx: **Revascularisation** (new blood supply) combines direct **STA-MCA bypass** (scalp to brain artery join) with indirect **EDAS** (artery laying operation) or muscle **synangiosis** (tissue fusion), and anaesthesia avoids hyperventilation, hypotension and crying that precipitate **ischaemia** (brain starvation) on the table, with aspirin continued perioperatively to protect graft patency.

steps.say: Company matters for screening. Down, NF1, sickle and thyroid disease travel with moyamoya, and one-sided disease usually turns bilateral.
steps.tx: Associations include **Down syndrome** (trisomy 21), **neurofibromatosis type 1** (nerve tumour illness), **sickle cell disease** (sickle blood illness) and thyroid disease, and unilateral early disease is watched closely because many cases show **bilateral progression** (both side spread) within years of diagnosis, with thyroid function tested because Graves disease coexists.

steps.say: A young woman with headache and fits after delivery is a sinus thrombosis until proven otherwise. The infarct pattern ignores arterial maps.
steps.tx: **Cerebral venous thrombosis** (sinus clot illness) strikes young women on **oral contraceptives** (birth control pills), pregnancy, postpartum or dehydration with headache, seizures and **papilloedema** (swollen eye disc), and haemorrhagic infarcts that do not respect arterial territories mark the venous cause.

vis.alt: Axial MRI and MR venography showing superior sagittal and transverse sinus thrombosis.
vis.caption: Venous sinus thrombosis on MRI and MR venography. Credit: Wolf et al. via Wikimedia Commons.

steps.say: The empty triangle on contrast CT is the giveaway. Loss of sinus flow on MR venography seals the diagnosis.
steps.tx: The **empty delta sign** (hollow triangle mark) on contrast CT and loss of flow void with sinus hyperintensity on **MRI-MRV** (vein scan) confirm thrombosis of the **superior sagittal sinus** (top midline channel) or transverse sinuses, and CT venography substitutes when MRI is unavailable overnight.

steps.say: Blood thinners treat clots even when the scan already shows blood. Withholding heparin for haemorrhage here kills.
steps.tx: **Heparin** (blood thinner) or low molecular weight heparin is started even when the infarct has **haemorrhagic transformation** (bleeding into stroke), followed by **warfarin** (long thinner) for **3 to 12 months** (three to twelve months), with **dabigatran** (newer thinner) an alternative after RESPECT-CVT suggested similar safety, supporting **heparin despite haemorrhage** (thinners with blood present).

steps.say: Deterioration on heparin escalates fast. Clot retrieval, local lysis and bone removal each have a rescue slot.
steps.tx: **Endovascular thrombectomy** (clot retrieval) or local thrombolysis is rescue therapy for deterioration despite heparin, and **decompressive hemicraniectomy** (half skull removal) saves life when a large **venous infarct** (vein stroke) herniates, with pressure monitoring guiding each escalation step and anticoagulation restarted once drains are out.
